122	that in truth, as Rav Ashlag, the Baal HaSulam, writes, there is nothing outside.
123	What does it mean, there is nothing outside?
124	It is all a projection of the rectifications we have to make within ourselves. Everything is projected
125	outside.
126	That is, if we see outside an enemy called Amalek, then yes, its rectifications
127	we do on the screen of reality.
128	There is nothing to be done.
129	"If one comes to kill you, rise early and kill him first."
130	The rectifications, the easier ones and the harder ones, we do
131	within reality.
132	That is, we are not only inside.
133	But it is also impossible to do the rectifications only outside.
134	We must blot out the memory of Amalek
135	from within us, and attain wholeness, clarity, joy
136	within us.
137	That comes first, or at least in parallel with the outer work.
138	So how can one truly be happy in such difficult days?
139	Because by the nature of things, as we said, it is very hard to be happy.
140	But the Jew is such a wonderful
141	creature
142	that he can live within nature, yet above nature.
143	That is, to be Yaakov, Yaakov's ladder, which is set on the ground, within
144	reality, with its head in the heavens.
145	Where did we first see this?
146	It is written, with the splitting of the Red Sea: "And the Children of Israel walked
147	on dry land in the midst of the sea."
148	What is "dry land in the midst of the sea"?
149	It comes to teach us the way a Jew can live.
150	Bnei Yisrael can live this way, as it is said of the tzaddik, "the tzaddik is the life of
151	the worlds."
152	A tzaddik can live in both worlds.
153	On one hand, to be in this world.
154	This world is likened to a sea.
155	Meaning what?
156	A sea: when you go to the sea or the ocean, what do you see?
